Temperatures this afternoon will begin to trail off on gusty northwest winds. The fall continues tonight with light rain showers changing to snow showers with top-down cooling cranking-up. Forecast Discussion

A cold front exited the mountain region this morning, only to be reinforced by a secondary front this evening. Light showers were mostly a morning thing before the secondary push of cold air tonight re-ignites upslope precipitation. Light rain showers will convert to snow showers overnight, chronologically occurring from west to east and from the ridgetops to the valleys.

Friday will feature snow showers and flurries, but accumulations will be limited to the western higher elevations, mostly above 3,500 feet in elevation. While snowflakes fall in the lower elevations, above-freezing surface temperatures will preclude accumulation.

Another surge of energy and cold air, aided by moisture transport off the Great Lakes, arrives Friday night. That is when the best opportunity for some light accumulations in lower elevation locales will occur.

Snow showers and flurries continue into Saturday morning before tapering off and ending by afternoon.

Here’s a reasonable model representation of forecast snowfall; Please look for our official snowfall forecast map, coming this afternoon.

This represents the coldest air of the fall season-to-date. Hard freezes are likely for Saturday, Sunday and Monday mornings.

After a chilly, dry start to the workweek, a slow moderation in temperatures commences with precipitation-free conditions.
